scope: Standalone historical-data analysis. Calculated estimates and engineering scenarios require separate review before any calibration use.

coverage.definition: Cumulative third lane adds limited credit for new, condition-qualified engineering coverage to the preceding augmented score. Historical scores are carried forward, including earlier credited derivations. Points reflect gap coverage and expert judgment.

credits.reason: Adds a source-anchored instantaneous lift boundary with altitude and coefficient sensitivity. Sustained performance remains open.
Adds a same-altitude net-power comparison at the two original ratings.
Adds narrow same-specimen IAS sensitivity from an actual stall mass, with a separate calibration assumption.
Adds three condition-matched relative installed-drag constraints with power-ratio sensitivity.
Adds two force-based lift boundaries with measured coefficient ranges for the exact specimen.
Adds a blower-specific net-power envelope and a consistent rate-integral check at reported combat settings.
Adds direct matched-power constraints on effective installation drag for distinct cooling settings.
Adds source-matched flight drag and L/D envelopes at two altitudes, limited by assumed installed efficiency.
Adds a condition-specific net-power envelope and qualifies separate D-9 radiator changes with scan bounds.
Adds paired cooling-state net-power constraints and estimates a missing elapsed-time interval.
Adds seven same-power installation drag constraints and an altitude-resolved comparison across three documented props.
Adds a documented exact-airframe sensitivity band with a separately stated anchor-weight and calibration scenario.
Adds a qualified period family-level climb schedule and a numerical consistency check. The exact captured aircraft remains without a completed climb trial.
Adds matched directional comparisons and bounded load interpretations for a documented control trial.
Expands the earlier single landing-weight calculation to a useful range, with a separately qualified original landing observation.
Adds a minimum-control-speed sensitivity constrained by same-specimen weight and fuel inventory. The separate Finnish aircraft retains its own condition set.
Adds a bounded, family-level drag plausibility check with the unresolved engine identification retained.

tables.title: Net climb power under the two Navy ratings
tables.note: BIS 2157 Plate 4 specifies 12,500 lb gross. Sea-level differences quantify the change in net climb power. Different power schedules and climb speeds can change both thrust and drag.

tables.title: Effective drag-area change from wing racks
tables.note: 15 May 1944, 75 inHg, 3,000 rpm. Match height, engine rating and gear per pair. Derived total effective area ratio assumes equal propulsive power. Sensitivity varies the power ratio by ±3% and speeds by ±0.5 mph. Includes induced drag and installation effects.

tables.title: Merlin 66 net power above level flight
tables.note: Uses the recorded 7,485 lb departure mass as the high scenario. The report used 95% of departure mass for its level-speed reductions. That fraction is a sensitivity case for climb, whose pointwise mass is unreported.

tables.title: Cooling-flap effective drag area relative to neutral
tables.note: 5,000 ft, 1,605 torque-meter bhp, 2,700 rpm. Equal propulsive power central estimate, ±3% sensitivity and ±0.5 mph source rounding. Effective total drag area includes lift and installation effects.

tables.title: Thirteen speed, power and effective drag constraints
tables.note: Quasi-steady level flight, L/D = W·V/(η·2·BHP). η = 0.70–0.85, chart shaft power ±5%, reported estimated weight ±2%. Analyst sensitivity ranges. Efficiency can vary with speed and RPM, so the curve gives conditional operating points.

tables.title: Conditional lift boundary versus buffet and abort
rows: Calculated, clean/off reference with fixed coefficient and proportional IAS calibration
tables.note: Power, true normal force, instantaneous mass, speed retention and flight path were unspecified in the turn. The comparison shows why it cannot constrain maximum sustained turn rate.

tables.title: Left/right steady-turn control compatibility
tables.note: Matched in label within 1 mph, altitude and CG. Fig. 25 reading allowance ±0.02 coefficient and ±0.2° elevator per marker. The lowest-speed pair shows the largest elevator offset. These are control points, with speed-basis, thrust and sustained limit unresolved.

tables.title: Nominal climb-power difference between cooling settings
tables.note: Net rate difference times nominal weight. Bounds span 95–100% of the recorded takeoff mass and independent ±0.35 m/s read windows. Cooling can affect thrust as well as drag.

tables.title: Nominal net climb power in the 3,000 rpm configuration
tables.note: Weight times recorded climb rate. Sensitivity to a 0–5% weight reduction from departure and the ±0.5 m/s chart window. Net climb power includes both thrust and aerodynamic drag. The separate 4,100 kg level trial supplies no climb mass.

tables.title: D-9 family cooling-setting differences at Rechlin
tables.note: Rechlin WNr 210006, 2,000 m, 2,700 rpm, empty external tank. Vw retained as printed. Reading allowance ±2 km/h per point. The test provides a separate installation tradeoff, with transfer to WNr 210002 unresolved.
